dod_intent_evidence: Plausible but stale and entirely self-asserted: their own 2021 BusinessWire release claims a 'Lattice-Based Data Protection Platform Validated by the United States Department of Defense' (news section). No contract number, no award record, and nothing in the last five years corroborates it.
score_evidence: Own-language word count is ~90 — far under the ~500-word floor. The entire website is one sentence plus a banner: 'Code-X Changes the foundation of security though proven innovative technology, eliminating the most vulnerable of attack surfaces and methodologies.' followed by 'GLOBAL COMMERCIAL RELEASE - 2026 / *Including a new website*'
The LinkedIn about section contains no product description at all — it is market-size boilerplate ('The digital economy accounts for 15–18% of global GDP (2025 estimates)')
No SBIR abstracts, no jobs data, and the three news items are all from 2021–2022 (the $5M Series A led by By Light, and an AWS partnership)

Per the gate, absence of deployment awareness only counts when the product is described in enough detail that deployment topics would naturally appear. Code-X describes no product. Scoring this high would be rewarding a company for saying nothing.
what_they_do: Claims a lattice-based data-protection platform for securing data and network packets; the public site is a placeholder promising a 2026 commercial release and a new website.
